_about: Terms shown as nodes on the home graph. Each term links to the pages that mention it (any alias, case-insensitive unless "case": true). Edit freely, then rerun tools/build_graph_site.py.

terms.label: Second brain
terms.def: One local folder of plain text that an agent reads and writes, holding what you have read and understood, that you can ask questions of.

terms.label: LLM wiki
terms.def: Karpathy's pattern: the model compiles sources into a linked wiki once, instead of rediscovering them from chunks on every question.

terms.label: Vault
terms.def: The folder of markdown the agent maintains. Obsidian calls it a vault; to the agent it is just files.

terms.label: Obsidian
terms.def: The markdown editor used to read the vault, browse its graph and clip sources. The agent never needs it running.

terms.label: Claude Code
terms.def: The agent that does the filing: reads raw sources, writes and links pages, runs the maintenance.

terms.label: CLAUDE.md
terms.def: Standing instructions the agent reads at the start of every session: who you are, the page contracts, the vault's rules.

terms.label: MCP
terms.def: Model Context Protocol: the standard plug that lets an agent reach tools and data, such as your vault from anywhere.

terms.label: raw/
terms.def: The inbox and archive: clipped articles, transcripts, PDFs. Written once, never edited, rarely read again.

terms.label: Two layers
terms.def: A wiki for what you know and a project layer for what you are doing, kept apart so each stays useful.

terms.label: Ingest
terms.def: Turning one raw source into linked wiki pages. Not finished until the new pages are connected to what was already there.

terms.label: Wikilink
terms.def: A [[Page name]] link between notes. The cheapest possible graph edge, and the reason the vault compounds.

terms.label: Backlinks
terms.def: The links pointing at a page. How you find everything that leans on an idea without searching for it.

terms.label: Atomic pages
terms.def: One idea per page, so a link means one thing and a page can be reused across every context it belongs to.

terms.label: Page types
terms.def: Source, concept, entity, synthesis: each with its own contract for what goes in it and how it links.

terms.label: Frontmatter
terms.def: The YAML block at the top of a page: type, sources, dates, status. What makes the vault queryable without a database.

terms.label: Aliases
terms.def: Other names a page answers to, so links and searches land on one page instead of spawning duplicates.

terms.label: Contradictions
terms.def: When a new source disagrees, both positions stay, dated and sourced. The record of what you believed and why.

terms.label: index.md and log.md
terms.def: The catalog the agent reads first, and one line per run so every change to the vault is auditable.

terms.label: Knowledge graph
terms.def: Pages as nodes, links as edges. In this setup the graph is the filesystem: no server, no separate store.

terms.label: Typed links
terms.def: A link that says how two pages relate, such as supports, contradicts or extends. Only typed when the source says so.

terms.label: Orphans
terms.def: Pages nothing links to. Invisible within a week, and the first number to watch when a vault is decaying.

terms.label: Hubs and bridges
terms.def: Hubs are pages everything links to; bridges connect clusters that would otherwise not touch. Both tell you where the thinking is.

terms.label: Clusters
terms.def: Groups of densely linked pages. The ones you did not plan are where the vault is telling you something.

terms.label: GraphRAG
terms.def: Retrieval over an extracted entity graph with community summaries. Built for global questions about a whole corpus.

terms.label: RAG
terms.def: Retrieval-augmented generation: fetch chunks by similarity at question time. Nothing accumulates between questions.

terms.label: Embeddings and vectors
terms.def: Similarity search over chunk embeddings. Worth adding only once a structured, linked vault stops answering.

terms.label: Context window
terms.def: What the model can see at once. Everything the agent knows in a session competes for this budget.

terms.label: Lost in the middle
terms.def: Models recall the start and end of a long context far better than the middle. Why stuffing everything in fails.

terms.label: Skills
terms.def: A folder with a SKILL.md: instructions the agent loads only when the task matches. One per workflow.

terms.label: Slash commands
terms.def: Short, scoped entry points into a skill, typed as /name. The handle you actually use day to day.

terms.label: Subagents
terms.def: Separate agents with their own context and a narrow tool list. Most of them here are read-only by design.

terms.label: Hooks
terms.def: Code the harness runs on events, before a tool call or after an edit. Rules the model cannot forget.

terms.label: Scheduled maintenance
terms.def: Lint, link and review runs on a timer, so the vault files itself while you sleep.

terms.label: Lint and health
terms.def: Mechanical checks for broken links, orphans, missing frontmatter and stale pages. The vault's test suite.

terms.label: Git
terms.def: Version history for the vault. Every agent run becomes reviewable and every bad run reversible.

terms.label: Privacy and secrets
terms.def: What must never reach a page, a prompt or a public export, and the checks that keep it out.

terms.label: Web Clipper
terms.def: Obsidian's browser extension. One click turns an article into a markdown file in raw/.

terms.label: Transcripts
terms.def: Video, voice and meetings turned into text so they can be ingested like anything else.

terms.label: Agent
terms.def: A model in a loop with tools, deciding its own next step until a goal is met or a stop rule fires.

terms.label: Five layers
terms.def: The course's frame for everything around the model: context, loop, gate, harness, evals.

terms.label: Workflows vs agents
terms.def: Code decides the next step in a workflow; the model decides in an agent. Most production systems are a hybrid.

terms.label: Context engineering
terms.def: Deciding what goes into the system prompt, tools, history and tail, and in what order, so the model sees the right things.

terms.label: Prompt caching
terms.def: Reusing the stable prefix of a prompt across calls. Cheaper and faster, if the context is laid out for it.

terms.label: Memory
terms.def: What persists between sessions. Here it is files the agent reads back, not a hidden feature of the model.

terms.label: Agent loop
terms.def: Goal, act, check, repeat. The loop is the control system around the model, and most failures live in it.

terms.label: Stop conditions
terms.def: When a loop must end: goal met, budget spent, no progress. A loop without one runs until it does damage.

terms.label: Critics and checkers
terms.def: A check outside the model that judges the result: tests, a compiler, a separate reviewer. Self-review is not one.

terms.label: The gate
terms.def: A cheap, narrow decision in front of an expensive model: one bounded question per item, route on the answer.

terms.label: System One models
terms.def: Small fast models that return typed decisions with confidence instead of text. Jev is one way to build the gate.

terms.label: Harness
terms.def: The office around the model: containment, guides, sensors and permissions, built from the outside in.

terms.label: Guardrails and permissions
terms.def: What the agent is allowed to touch, what it must ask about, and the walls that hold when it is wrong.

terms.label: Tool use
terms.def: The model asking the harness to run something on its behalf. Every capability an agent has arrives this way.

terms.label: Evals
terms.def: The same test, every month: checks on real behaviour so a prompt or model change cannot quietly break things.

terms.label: Golden set
terms.def: The fixed collection of cases every eval runs against, including the failures you have already seen.

terms.label: LLM as judge
terms.def: A model grading outputs against a rubric. Useful once the judge itself has been checked against human labels.

terms.label: Traces
terms.def: The full record of what an agent did, step by step. What behavioural evals and debugging both read.

terms.label: Production
terms.def: The step from a demo that works once to a system with tracing, cost control, security and an owner.
